primitives.name: SHAP Feature Contribution Explainability
primitives.verbatim_quote: SHAP-style explainability is the mechanism that satisfies both — explain WHY a pick was made (feature contributions) without revealing the model.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S_i': 'SHAP value for feature i (dimensionless)', 'f(x)': 'model prediction function', 'x_i': 'input feature i'}
primitives.assumptions: Model is additive; marginal contribution of features is independent.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When model complexity exceeds linear approximation, SHAP values become unreliable.

layer2.mapping: SHAP kernel encodes feature importance for trust-building; GSI uses it to generate public explanations for internal decisions.
layer2.telemetry: Trust score derived from explanation clarity and alignment with outcome

primitives.name: Motion Skills Verification Loop
primitives.verbatim_quote: The 54 skills matter less than the deliver-and-verify loop: render a frame, screenshot it, check it.
primitives.assumptions: Agent produces artifacts with deterministic output structure; verification is binary.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When V < 0.9, verification becomes unreliable due to noise in rendering process.

layer2.mapping: Verify loop ensures artifact quality before deployment; GSE applies this to all agent-generated content.
layer2.telemetry: Artifact pass/fail ratio, time to verification completion

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that GSI and GSE operate under dual constraints: GSI must maintain trust through explainability while GSE must ensure correctness through verification. The RAG layer enables GSI to surface insights from a corpus, but only if those insights are interpretable via SHAP. Meanwhile, GSE’s motion-skills loop ensures that generated content meets a quality bar before release. These primitives form a closed-loop system where trust (GSI) and correctness (GSE) reinforce each other. Failure modes include: RAG degradation when corpus grows beyond retrieval limits, SHAP misalignment when model complexity increases, and verification bypass when thresholds are too lenient. The interplay between these systems reflects a deeper duality: interpretability as a constraint and verification as a mechanism for overcoming it.
